prompt: Sort each digital touchpoint below into Owned Media, Paid Media, or Earned Media.

cards.text: A running-shoe brand updates its mobile training app and product catalog on its e-commerce storefront.
cards.explanation: Owned media consist of digital properties that the brand controls directly, such as its corporate website, e-commerce storefront, and mobile application.

cards.text: A coffee roaster sends a weekly brewing guide to its opted-in email subscriber list.
cards.explanation: An opted-in email subscriber list and company blog are owned media assets controlled directly by the brand.

cards.text: A luggage company pays per click for a sponsored listing at the top of a search engine results page.
cards.explanation: Paid media consist of external digital placements for which the brand pays to acquire reach and traffic, including paid search advertisements.

cards.text: A skincare label pays a creator a sponsorship fee to feature its moisturizer in a promoted social video.
cards.explanation: Paid influencer sponsorships and paid social-media promotions are external placements bought to acquire reach.

cards.text: A verified buyer posts an unprompted five-star review and photo of a camping tent on an outdoor forum.
cards.explanation: Earned media consist of organic exposure generated voluntarily by consumers through customer reviews and forum recommendations.

cards.text: A technology journalist includes a brand's wireless keyboard in an independent roundup of home-office gear.
cards.explanation: Unpaid press coverage and independent creator mentions are earned media that supply third-party credibility.

prompt: For each search marketing action or outcome below, identify whether it describes Search Engine Optimization (SEO) or Search Engine Marketing (SEM).

cases.text: A meal-kit company bids on the phrase 'quick weeknight dinners' in a real-time auction so its sponsored link appears above organic results today.
cases.explanation: SEM involves bidding on specific keywords in real-time ad auctions to place a sponsored listing above or beside organic search results.

cases.text: A financial-planning firm improves page loading speed, clarifies technical metadata, and publishes tax guides that university websites link to.
cases.explanation: SEO structures web pages, technical metadata, site speed, and authoritative content with external backlinks to rank higher in unpaid organic results.

cases.text: A retailer's top-of-page visibility begins the hour its campaign budget turns on and disappears the moment daily spending is paused.
cases.explanation: SEM delivers immediate visibility when a budget is active and stops as soon as spending stops.

cases.text: After six months of publishing authoritative repair guides, a bicycle shop receives steady daily search visitors without paying a per-click ad fee.
cases.explanation: SEO requires months of sustained investment but compounds into durable organic traffic without a per-click advertising fee.

prompt: Match each automated email lifecycle trigger with the customer action that initiates it.

pairs.match: A new visitor creates an account and opts in to the mailing list, receiving an introduction to the brand's core products.
pairs.explanation: A welcome sequence is triggered automatically right after account creation or newsletter opt-in.

pairs.match: A shopper adds a winter coat to her online bag and closes the browser tab before paying, receiving a helpful follow-up link.
pairs.explanation: An abandoned-cart trigger sends a timely reminder after a shopper leaves items in a cart without completing checkout.

pairs.match: Two days after a cast-iron skillet arrives at a buyer's home, the brand emails seasoning and cleaning instructions.
pairs.explanation: A post-delivery trigger sends helpful onboarding or care instructions once a product is delivered.

pairs.match: Twenty-five days after a customer buys a thirty-day supply of contact lenses, the retailer sends a one-click reorder message.
pairs.explanation: A replenishment prompt is timed to arrive when a consumable item is due to run out.

prompt: Match each social media platform category with the marketing objective and usage norm it fits best.

pairs.match: Showcasing interior-design aesthetics, fashion lookbooks, and recipe photography during early inspiration and consideration.
pairs.explanation: Visual discovery platforms such as Instagram and Pinterest excel at showcasing aesthetics, fashion, food, and home design.

pairs.match: Using algorithmic interest graphs to reach younger and mainstream audiences with rapid product demonstrations.
pairs.explanation: Short-form video platforms such as TikTok and YouTube Shorts rely on algorithmic interest graphs for rapid organic reach and product demonstrations.

pairs.match: Publishing B2B thought leadership, connecting with enterprise executives, and running account-based marketing campaigns.
pairs.explanation: Professional networks such as LinkedIn support B2B thought leadership, executive networking, and account-based marketing.

pairs.match: Reading candid, long-form peer product evaluations and troubleshooting threads written by hobbyists and owners.
pairs.explanation: Discussion forums such as Reddit host detailed peer product evaluations and community discussions.

prompt: Match each digital marketing metric or evaluation concept with its definition.

pairs.match: The number of ad clicks divided by the total number of impressions.
pairs.explanation: Click-through rate measures the share of impressions that result in a click.

pairs.match: The number of completed purchases divided by the number of clicks.
pairs.explanation: Conversion rate measures the share of visitors who complete the target action such as a purchase.

pairs.match: A surface figure such as raw follower count or post likes that looks impressive on a slide but does not correlate with sales or retention.
pairs.explanation: Vanity metrics look impressive in reports but fail to reflect incremental revenue or customer retention.

pairs.match: A test comparing conversion rates between an exposed group and an unexposed control group to measure true causal incrementality.
pairs.explanation: Randomized holdout experiments isolate the causal incremental lift of a digital campaign beyond organic baseline sales.

question_text: An electronics brand assumes that because AI shopping agents are software programs, they will evaluate all fifty laptops on a marketplace page equally regardless of rank order. What do the controlled experiments of Wadi and Ma (2026a) show about this assumption?
hint: Consider how rank order in a candidate list affects AI shopping agent selection even when attributes and prices are held constant.
correct_answer_citation: Week 11: List Position Effects When AI Agents Search (Wadi & Ma, 2026a)

options.option_text: AI shopping agents evaluate every item on a page with equal probability regardless of rank position.
options.option_explanation: Empirical studies show the opposite: software agents do not weigh every rank position equally.

options.option_text: AI shopping agents exhibit strong position effects, favoring options because of where they appear in a ranked list even when objective attributes and prices are held constant.
options.option_explanation: Correct. Controlled experiments demonstrate that AI shopping agents exhibit strong position effects, making top rank placement in marketplace feeds critical (Wadi & Ma, 2026a).

options.option_text: Rank order only affects human shoppers browsing physical store shelves and has no effect on software agents.
options.option_explanation: AI shopping agents read ranked product lists and exhibit pronounced position effects of their own (Wadi & Ma, 2026a).

options.option_text: AI shopping agents ignore structured marketplace feeds and only read video commercials.
options.option_explanation: AI shopping agents directly parse ranked product lists and structured data indices when searching on a consumer's behalf.

question_text: In experiments testing how AI shopping agents react to paid placement disclosure labels on ranked product lists, how did the wording of the label affect agent choice (Wadi & Ma, 2026c)?
hint: Compare how often AI agents selected an identical paid listing when it was labeled 'Sponsored' versus 'Promoted'.
correct_answer_citation: Week 11: Sponsored Labels and Paid Placements in Agent-Mediated Search (Wadi & Ma, 2026c)

options.option_text: AI agents selected listings labeled 'Sponsored' much more often than listings labeled 'Promoted'.
options.option_explanation: The experimental effect ran in the opposite direction: the 'Sponsored' label triggered stronger avoidance than 'Promoted' (Wadi & Ma, 2026c).

options.option_text: Disclosure label wording had zero effect on AI agent choices because agents strip out all badge text.
options.option_explanation: AI agents read disclosure labels in ranked lists, and the exact wording significantly alters selection rates (Wadi & Ma, 2026c).

options.option_text: AI agents chose a paid listing less often when it was labeled 'Sponsored' than when the identical paid listing was labeled 'Promoted'.
options.option_explanation: Correct. The exact wording of the disclosure label significantly alters agent choice, with 'Sponsored' reducing selection more than 'Promoted' (Wadi & Ma, 2026c).

options.option_text: Regulators prohibit paid listings from carrying any disclosure labels when shown to human or AI searchers.
options.option_explanation: Regulators require clear disclosure labels so searchers can distinguish paid advertisements from organic rankings.
